First, note that the range of $\theta =\operatorname{arcsin}⁡x$ is given by

$$
-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Now, let's take a look at the unit circle.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13964047/assets/a33ea7c6d1aa7cd7e54376aefb2af4347da59a61ecaabdbf4964d41b9661870a.png)

From the values in the unit circle, we see that

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3})=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

However, $\frac{5\pi }{3}$ does not lie within the range of $\theta .$ To get an angle that's coterminal with $\frac{5\pi }{3}$ that lies within the range of $\theta ,$ we subtract $2\pi .$

$$
\frac{5\pi }{3}-2\pi =-\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

Hence,

$$
arcsin\,(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=-\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9arcsin\,(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) & =9(-\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =-3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
